title: Vernon Andrade's band at the Renaissance
summary: Andrade led a house band where musicians like Howard Johnson and Fats Green worked between better jobs, with no ambition beyond steady work.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

blocks.x: With one band or two?

Well, they had one band, and two bands on special occasions. But they would have one band as a general rule. I can't think of the fellow's name who used to be the bandleader there. He stayed there for years.
Well, Vernon Andrade was the...
Andrade. Vernon Andrade. He was the leader of the band. He stayed there for years. Yeah, Vernon Andrade, that's right.
It seems like if you hung around Harlem long enough, you'd eventually work for him.

Yeah, eventually you'd wind up working for him. That's right. Because I mean, they were coming and going in his band all the time. I mean, his band, he had no aspirations for going any place or doing anything. But he had a job. And that was the name of the game in them days -- a job. So different fellows, they'd be working or rehearsing in the big-time bands. Like Chick Webb's band, you'd be rehearsing with Chick Webb, but Chick wasn't doing anything, so they'd go to work with Vernon Andrade until the other band found something to do. And they were always in and out of Andrade's band. It didn't seem to faze him none. As long as you could play the music, that was the main thing with him.
What did he play himself? Or did he?
He had a guitar.
But he fronted the bands mostly?
Well, it was his band. It was nothing elaborate about it or spectacular. He sat down and played his guitar, and the rest of the band just played the music.
Did he arrange?
No.
Or compose?
No.
What did he do? Stocks then mostly?
That's right. Stocks, or somebody had something they wanted to play, then...
I think he came from the Islands? The West Indies? [PANAMA]

Mmm-hmm. And he had some good musicians who worked for him down through the years. Some of the best in the business worked for him. They were glad to get the jobs. Yeah, some terrific saxophone players worked for him. Howard Johnson worked for him for years. Another fellow named Fats Green. He could play all of the reeds, and I mean he could play it. He was terrific.
Do you remember where Fats Green was from?
No. He was from around here somewhere. Fats Green had a band of his own. Later on he got plenty of
work around Harlem.
What was his main instrument? Alto?

Alto... Saxophones. He played all the saxophones. Clarinet. A very good clarinetist. Yeah, Fats was very good. He had a lot of good musicians in Andrade's band. In fact, some of the best musicians. I even think Buster Bailey was with him at one time. You name 'em, they had worked for Andrade. Sure.
And he never toured or anything.
No.
He just stayed at the Renny.
He just stayed right there. He wasn't thinking about going no place. He was just one of them kind of guys he had a job, and that was good enough for him. He wasn't trying to elaborate on anything.
